canDo: Can state limits precisely with structures such as ne…que / aucun / ni…ni while keeping a complaint polite.
review: Review basic negation, pronouns and the conditionnel; extend to B1 negation.
input: Listening and reading on housing problems/repair notices.
output: Write a 140-word complaint email; a 3-minute spoken exchange with a landlord.
checkpoint: Specific facts, a clear impact, an explicit request, an appropriate tone.
challenge: Today’s challenge: think of a real problem in a place you’ve lived (noise, a leak, the heating…) and write a polite 6-sentence complaint using ne…que, aucun and ni…ni at least once each; end with a specific request for a remedy and a deadline.

questions.why: He quotes « le règlement de copropriété, à l'article 12 ».
« vérifier si l'erreur ne s'étend pas aux trimestres précédents », admitting he doesn’t have the old statements to hand.
« plutôt que d'avoir à inscrire ce point à l'ordre du jour » — giving the other side a face-saving way out.
Three weeks without a reply to the registered letter; a settlement was offered eight days after the summons from the conciliation committee.
The service department points out that the legal conformity guarantee is two years, not one.
« S'il devait être dépassé, un appareil de prêt vous serait proposé, sur simple demande » — two conditions combined.
It accepts the repair request and also corrects what was said about the length of the guarantee.
The contrasting examples show that only specific dates and times correspond to rules that can be checked.
« Je ne veux pas une quatrième réparation identique, je veux un diagnostic complet ». Payment only comes up once the diagnosis is known.
« on ne va pas commencer à photographier les voitures des gens, ce n'est pas notre rôle », and the other side also denies having suggested it.
Both demands are met: next month’s bill adjusted + the Tuesday slot, confirmed by text that evening.
By June, a January bill no longer meets the “within three months” requirement.
